question: A grocer bought 20 kg of wheat type P at 50 per kg and 30 kg of wheat type Q at 80 per kg. He mixed them and sold the entire mixture at 70 per kg. Calculate his total profit or loss.
solution:
**Given:**

Quantity of wheat type P = 20 kg

Cost price of wheat type P = ₹50/kg

Quantity of wheat type Q = 30 kg

Cost price of wheat type Q = ₹80/kg

Selling price of mixture = ₹70/kg

**Formula Used:**

Total cost price = (Quantity of type P × Cost price of type P) + (Quantity of type Q × Cost price of type Q)

Total selling price = Total quantity × Selling price per kg

Profit/Loss = Total selling price - Total cost price

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total cost price = (20 × 50) + (30 × 80)

⇒ Total cost price = ₹1000 + ₹2400

⇒ Total cost price = ₹3400

⇒ Total quantity = 20 + 30

⇒ Total quantity = 50 kg

⇒ Total selling price = 50 × 70

⇒ Total selling price = ₹3500

⇒ Profit/Loss = ₹3500 - ₹3400

⇒ Profit = ₹100

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 100.**
